TechAfrica News says the Malawi government has launched the Malawi Low Resource Language Data Trust Initiative to develop Chichewa AI models and assemble licensed Chichewa content, supported by the World Bank and the Gates Foundation.

fact: iAfrica.com reports AGRA's MlimiVoice Malawi, an agriculture language-AI project, is among 26 projects selected under LINGUA Africa, funded by the Microsoft AI for Good Lab, Gates Foundation, Masakhane African Languages Hub and Google.org with up to $250,000 cash and $400,000 compute credits per awardee.

The CREWS note says MET Norway, with WMO funding of USD 250,000, will adapt the Bris AI weather model to the Malawi domain and install it at DCCMS, with USD 18,000 for computing hardware to run it, over May to October 2025.

ITWeb Africa reports that Converged Technology Networks (CTN) has announced plans to build Malawi's first Micro Data Centre for AI computing, with NVIDIA A100 GPUs to be installed 'in the coming months' and rented as a service.

The Malawi Voice Data Commons, built by NYU and Mozilla with Malawian universities, fine-tunes OpenAI's Whisper model on newly collected Chichewa data and runs local servers for real-time keyword detection and transcription of emergency reports, cutting response times from 72 to 6 hours, per Portulans Institute.

The University of Malawi says it leads development and validation of an AI model for an agrometeorological advisory system under the NORAD-backed ARCS initiative, which was in expert review and farmer pretesting in September 2026.

A World Bank work plan for June 2026 to July 2027 transfers a Chichewa language data trust, built in an earlier phase on World Bank infrastructure from Malawian media archives and National Statistical Office recordings, to the Malawi Research and Education Network (MAREN) to run, with public launch staged for the Geneva AI Summit 2027.
